purpose: P4 lossless performance baseline — measured on isolated restored instance (185:/mnt/data1/l2_restore, PG16.4, wal_level=minimal)
status: MEASURED (restored instance, cold-ish cache post-restore; prod warm cache typically faster)

workloads.W2_single_asset_factor_series: SELECT trade_date,factor_name,factor_value FROM factor.factor_daily WHERE asset_id='CN:SH:600111' AND factor_name=$chosen ORDER BY trade_date DESC LIMIT 2000
workloads.W3_backtest_batch: SELECT trade_date,asset_id,factor_value FROM factor.factor_daily WHERE factor_name=$chosen AND calc_version='v1' AND trade_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-10-27' ORDER BY trade_date,asset_id
workloads.W4_minute_bar_range: SELECT * FROM market.stock_minute_bar WHERE trade_date BETWEEN '2026-10-20' AND '2026-10-27' AND asset_id=$chosen
workloads.W5_multi_factor_screen: SELECT asset_id, factor_name, factor_value FROM factor.factor_daily WHERE trade_date='2026-10-27' AND factor_name IN ($top5)
workloads.W6_eod_incremental: SELECT max(trade_date), count(*) FROM factor.factor_daily WHERE trade_date >= current_date - 7

measurement: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) x3 runs; record plan+exec_ms+buffers; identical results verified by rowcount+md5

W2_single_asset_factor_series.note: index serves shape; cost dominated by 75GB heap+TOAST random fetches, NOT index traversal

W3_backtest_batch.note: 1M fat-row heap fetches dominate; index choice already optimal

W4_minute_bar_range.note: freq value is '5min'; partition pruning works

results.insight: slow queries are payload-bound (610M rows x ~120B fat rows), not index-bound; storage efficiency fix = row width/density, not index deletion

index_bloat_evidence.method: pg_relation_size prod vs freshly-restored build (identical definition)
